name: transactions
description: A MUTATE block is one transaction, not a script that happens to run in order: everything in it commits or none of it does. A precondition that fails leaves the element exactly as the caller last saw it. EXPECT VERSION is the one guard, and it is always the trailing clause (Spec §52.8); there is no EXPECT STATE — TRANSITION validates the target's current lifecycle state itself and fails InvalidLifecycleTransition from the wrong one (§35.3, §52.5), while a move to the state already held is a no_effect rather than an error.

cases.name: an omitted assertion time defaults to the engine transaction time
cases.command: FIND(COUNT(?a)) WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} FILTER(?a.asserted_at >= "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z") }

cases.name: a clause that fails undoes the clauses that already ran beside it
so the clause that succeeded left nothing behind
cases.command: FIND(COUNT(?c)) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {name: "Rollback probe"} }

cases.name: a stale EXPECT VERSION refuses the write
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?p { MATCH {key: "person:alice"} SET FIELDS {name: "Rewritten"} } EXPECT VERSION 99

cases.name: and the refused write changed nothing
cases.command: FIND(?c.name) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: a selection block that matches nothing is a no-op, not an error
cases.command: UPDATE ?c SET ATTRIBUTES { note: "unreachable" } WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {name: "Nobody"} }

cases.name: TRANSITION validates the move against the target's kind: an Assertion has no Activity state to move to
cases.command: TRANSITION ?a TO "running" WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: the claim it refused to touch is still active
cases.command: FIND(?a.lifecycle.status) WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: the assertor's withdrawal is one TRANSITION, legal from active
cases.command: TRANSITION ?a TO "retracted" WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: and the claim is withdrawn rather than deleted
cases.command: FIND(?a.lifecycle.status, ?a.confidence) WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: a move to the state the target already holds is no_effect, not an error
cases.command: TRANSITION ?a TO "retracted" WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: and a move that is not legal from retracted is refused
cases.command: TRANSITION ?a TO "superseded" BY "A-1" WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} }

cases.name: a stale guard on one version plane names the plane it refused
cases.command: UPDATE ?c SET ATTRIBUTES { note: "late" } WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} } EXPECT VERSION 99 OF ATTRIBUTES

cases.name: the same guard on two planes is refused as syntax, before anything runs
cases.command: UPDATE ?c SET ATTRIBUTES { note: "late" } WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} } EXPECT VERSION 1 OF ATTRIBUTES EXPECT VERSION 1 OF ATTRIBUTES

cases.name: a guard between the target and the actions is not where a mutation keeps its preconditions
cases.command: UPDATE ?c EXPECT VERSION 1 SET ATTRIBUTES { note: "late" } WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: a CLIENT KEY retry writes nothing and hands back the element the first attempt made
so the same creation under the same key is a retry, not a second Casey
and there is one of them
cases.command: FIND(COUNT(?c)) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {type: "Person", name: "Casey"} }

cases.name: but a different creation under that key is a conflict, never a silent reuse
two clauses that give one target two final values have no answer but a refusal
and the refused block changed nothing
cases.command: FIND(?c.name) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

cases.name: two clauses that agree are not in conflict: a plan assembled from parts may say a thing twice
nor are two clauses writing different paths of one target
so the two writes that agreed and the two that did not overlap both landed
cases.command: FIND(?c.name, ?c.attributes.role) WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {key: "person:alice"} }

Option.description: A preference option used by these fixtures. A real Space types each option by its kind (Profile §5.5, §7), because prefers partitions by the option's Concept Type; one catch-all type is one partition.
